messages:
Maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's modelpack deployment I'm seeing a consistent eval delta on structured outputs when using FP8/INT8 mixed kernels. Small but real: schema fields get shuffled or dropped in ~2.7% of test prompts (compare to FP32 baseline).
Devin: Ugh. Is this the new kernel selector fallback we rolled last week? :thinking_face:
Maria: Possibly. Profiling shows the runtime picked an INT8 matmul kernel for attention at seq_len=512, but for smaller sequences it used a different 4-bit-packed kernel. The calibration step also switched from dynamic to static for that variant.
Owen: Do you have perf traces + diffed logits? If schema is breaking that sounds like quantization noise, not batching.
Maria: I dumped a tiny repro and logs. Key bits below:

```
# repro loop
prompt = 'Generate a json list of users with id, name, email'
model: gpt-small-v2.quant.fp8+int8
batch=1
seq=128

# runtime log
[2026-06-01T08:12:03Z] kernel_select: matmul_int8_fast (gpu:0)
[2026-06-01T08:12:03Z] kernel_select_fallback: matmul_4bit_packed for seq<256
[2026-06-01T08:12:03Z] kvcache: miss_rate=0.18
[2026-06-01T08:12:03Z] calibration: static (calib_set=calib_v2_small)
```

The generated JSONs sometimes miss closing commas or reorder fields (`email` <-> `id`). I compared raw logits and saw token-prob shifts of ~0.6-1.2 logits on key separators (commas, braces).
Devin: Token-prob shifts that big can definitely break structured output. Did the calibration set differ from the eval prompts?
Maria: Yes. calib_v2_small was collected from short-chat data (seq<64). The eval set is a structured-output corpus with longer tokens and field names. Suspect calibration distribution mismatch + kernel mismatch.
Owen: Also check KV cache behavior — if the KV cache path is using fp16 cache but kernels expect int8-packed keys, misalignment could scramble attention offsets.
Leah: Any perf regressions alongside quality issues? We need to know if this is performance-opt or correctness.
Maria: Perf-wise: throughput improved 1.9x for long sequences using INT8 kernels, p50 latency down, but p99 regressed for small batches when fallback switched kernels. Numbers:

```
baseline fp32: p50=120ms, p99=320ms, tokens/s=250
quant mixed: p50=65ms, p99=420ms, tokens/s=470
```

So overall more throughput but tail latency and correctness issues.
Samir: Do we have kernel canonicalization logs? Which kernels were chosen across steps?
Maria: Yes — I exported kernel traces across 200 requests. Snapshot:

- seq<=128: matmul_4bit_packed (fast path for small seq) + static calibration
- seq 129-384: matmul_int8_fast
- seq>384: intel-fp8-optim kernel

The weird part: when switching kernels mid-session (due to variable prompt lengths) we saw KV cache eviction and a small frequency of stale cache reads (rare) — those correlate with the broken outputs.
Owen: That sounds like a concurrency bug in KV cache tagging when dtype/shape changes. If kv keys are stored with dtype tag A and then read assuming tag B you'll see attention index misreads.
Devin: Can you reproduce with a deterministic tiny script that alternates short/long prompts to force kernel switches? Also include --no-cache run to see if KV cache is the cause.
Maria: I built a minimal repro that alternates seq=32 and seq=256 prompts with same conversation id. Results:
- With KV cache ON: 2.6% bad outputs
- With KV cache OFF: 0.1% bad outputs
So KV cache seems necessary for the bug.
Leah: Great repro. That strongly implicates cache dtype/shape tagging.
Samir: Calibration still matters — static calibration from small sequences probably underflows/quantizes certain tokens poorly. Could explain token-prob shifts too.
Owen: Action items:
1) I will instrument KV cache to include kernel-version and dtype tags + checksums and add asserts in debug builds. (assign: Owen)
2) Re-run calibration with a mixed-length calibration set that mirrors structured-output tokens. (assign: Maria)
3) Add a unit test to reproduce alternating seqs with cache on and assert identical outputs to cache-off. (assign: Devin)
4) Short-term mitigation: pin kernel to int8-only for structured-output models via runtime policy and disable the 4bit packed fallback. (assign: Leah)

Devin: For the int8 pinning, can we route requests by route-tag? Product can add a model_config flag to force kernel family in runtime.
Leah: Yep. We can expose kernel_policy in model-config: {preferred_kernels: ["int8_fast"], fallback: "fp32"}
Samir: FYI QA reported some hallucinations increase in the same timeframe — I suspect both calibration and KV bug together amplify errors.
Maria: Timeline: Owen will push debug build with extra kv tags today. Maria will push new calibration set and rerun eval tomorrow. Leah will prepare kernel_policy patch for deploy-canary.
ci-bot: canary build 2026-06-01-17:45 queued. logs: https://ci.internal/canaries/4521
Owen: Quick note — the checksum asserts will be opt-in via env REDWOOD_KV_STRICT=true to avoid perf hit in prod.
Devin: Once we have reproducer, please add perf traces (nvprof / nsight) and include kernel timings for matmul, kv-read, kv-write.
Maria: Will attach full trace + diffs to this thread after today's run. For now I pushed the simple repro script to /infra/repros/fp8-kv-alt-seq.py
Samir: Thx all. If QE sees the kernel_policy mitigation reduces deltas we can roll it to canary and then gradully enable strict kv checks in staging.
Leah: I'll take care of canary rollout plan. :thumbsup:
Owen: Starting instrumentation now. ETA 6h.
Maria: Update: quick dry-run — switching calibration to mixed-length cut bad outputs to 0.8% (from 2.7%). So calibration mismatch was a big factor.
Devin: That's promising. Keep KV checks on priority.
Samir: Tagging security: @leah for kernel_policy change — make sure model config change has no new attack surface (public UI editable?).
Leah: Will gate it behind enterprise-only flag for now.
Maria: I'll post the eval diffs after next run. Thanks team.
